deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Let U = P^1_C \ {0,1,∞}. Let Γ = S_{0,1,∞} × Z/2 ≅ S_3 × Z/2 be the group of holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms of U, with τ: z ↦ z̄. Let E = E_{0,3} be the extension 1 → Π → E → Γ → 1, where Π = π_1(U) is free on ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ with ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1. Equivalently, E is the orbifold fundamental group of [U/Γ]. Classically this is PGL_2(Z), the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group: Π = Γ(2)/±1 and S_3 = PSL_2(F_2).

Grothendieck's programme here is to classify the Π-conjugacy classes of maximal 'scindages partiels'. These are splittings of E over finite subgroups G ⊂ Γ. He does this through fixed points of G on U, and through connected components of fixed loci of antiholomorphic elements. This is the discrete, topological prototype of the (real and finite-group) section conjecture.

Previous page. The fixed points P = e^{iπ/3} and P̄ have stabilizer of order 6 (≅ S_3). Their lifts are conjugate under E. He then takes σ̇_0, the involution z ↦ z/(z−1). It fixes 0 and swaps 1 and ∞. Its only fixed point in U is z = 2, with stabilizer ⟨σ̇_0, τ⟩ ≅ (Z/2)^2.

This page.
- **Lifting at z = 2.** Work on the Riemann sphere with 0, 1, ∞ on a great circle (the real line). Use the quarter great circle joining P to the point 2, the midpoint of the arc (1,∞) opposite 0. This path identifies the universal cover based at P with the one based at the point 2. The stabilizer acts canonically on the latter, so by transport of structure it acts on Ũ(P). This gives a homomorphism of the stabilizer into E, i.e. a partial splitting.
- **Explicit lift.** The result is σ̇_0 ↦ σ_0, τ ↦ τ_0.
- **The other two points.** The same is done at the fixed point −1 of σ̇_1 (z ↦ 1/z) and at the fixed point 1/2 of σ̇_∞ (z ↦ 1−z). He names these points 0' = 2, 1' = −1, ∞' = 1/2. Their isotropy groups Γ_{0'} = ⟨σ̇_0, τ⟩, Γ_{1'} = ⟨σ̇_1, τ⟩, Γ_{∞'} = ⟨σ̇_∞, τ⟩ lift respectively to ⟨σ_0, τ_0⟩, ⟨σ_1, τ_1⟩, ⟨σ_∞, τ_∞⟩.
- **Real components.** U^τ has three components, the real arcs (−∞,0), (0,1), (1,∞). Each contains exactly one of 0', 1', ∞'. So the three conjugacy classes of splittings over {1,τ} (completed on the next page) are the classes of τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞. These are 'nothing new' beyond the restrictions of the Klein-four splittings.
- **Next page.** The remaining case τσ̇_1 (and its conjugates) yields nothing new either. Grothendieck then starts writing a presentation of E by generators and relations.

In modern terms, the page establishes:
- the maximal finite subgroups of E ≅ PGL_2(Z) are, up to conjugacy, one D_3 (at P) and three Klein four-groups (at 0', 1', ∞', permuted by S_3), in line with the classical amalgam PGL_2(Z) ≅ D_2 *_{Z/2} D_3;
- the conjugacy classes of real sections correspond bijectively to the three components of U(R).

The purpose is the 'Lego' of the extended Teichmüller tower in the spirit of the Esquisse. The torsion and the real structures of the building block E_{0,3} are needed in order to glue the higher E_{g,n}, and later to compare with the profinite/Galois version.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The checks hold: z/(z−1) fixes 0 and 2; 1/z fixes ±1; 1−z fixes 1/2 and ∞; and −1, 1/2, 2 lie in (−∞,0), (0,1), (1,∞) respectively, one per real arc.
The phrase 'Γ_1 ⊂ Γ et Γ_2 ⊂ Γ' is presumably shorthand for the isotropy groups Γ_{1'} and Γ_{∞'}; the indexing is loose.
The transcription's 'l'arc (0,∞) ... opposé à 0' is inconsistent. The arc opposite 0 is (1,∞), whose midpoint is 2, and the manuscript itself reads (1,∞).

ideas.what: Classifying conjugacy classes of partial splittings of the extension 1→π_1(U)→E→Aut^±(U)→1 over finite subgroups via fixed points (and components of fixed loci for antiholomorphic elements).
ideas.modern_name: Discrete/orbifold section correspondence; fixed points ↔ conjugacy classes of finite subgroups (Nielsen realization, Smith theory). Topological prototype of the section conjecture.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for discrete groups (Nielsen, Kerckhoff for realization); real section conjecture: Mochizuki, Pál, Wickelgren and others (2000s).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of finite subgroups of Teichmüller groups and real/discrete analogues); letter to Faltings 1983 (section conjecture, real case mentioned).

ideas.what: Explicit lifts of the Klein four isotropy groups ⟨σ̇_i, τ⟩ at the points 2, −1, 1/2 via quarter great-circle paths from the base point P = e^{iπ/3}.
ideas.modern_name: Maximal finite subgroups of PGL_2(Z) (the D_2 vertex of PGL_2(Z) ≅ D_2 *_{Z/2} D_3); tangential/path base-point transport.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (structure of PGL_2(Z) as the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group).

ideas.what: The three conjugacy classes of real splittings (lifts of τ) correspond to the three components of U(R) = the three real arcs, each containing exactly one of the points 0', 1', ∞'.
ideas.modern_name: Real section correspondence for P^1 minus 3 points (discrete version).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in topological form; arithmetic real section conjecture: Mochizuki, Pál (2011), Wickelgren.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but classical computations of the finite subgroups and real sections of E_{0,3} ≅ PGL_2(Z), via orbifold fixed points. They are a worked instance of a programme Grothendieck sketched publicly in the Esquisse; nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'l'arc (0,∞)' should read 'l'arc (1,∞)': the arc opposite 0, with midpoint 2.
'revêtement universel de M en P' should be 'de U en P'.
'Je ... commence[?] de pas[?] F' is likely 'Je ... [il est] commode de poser'; the 'F' appears to be a stray or struck mark.
Last line: 'contenant chacun un et un seul des pts 0', 1', ∞'' (the struck word is not 'pt').
'd'où aussi par transport de structure sur Ũ(P), donc il s'envoie dans E': the reading Ũ(P) is plausible, over a struck correction.
